# Hooks for your own stylesheet

A stylesheet of your own (`custom.css` in the data folder; [custom-css.md](custom-css.md) says how it is loaded) may restyle anything on the page. What it can rely on from one release to the next is this list, and only this list: the tokens, the attributes on the page’s root, the parts, and the attributes on some parts. A hook is only ever added; none is renamed or removed. The list is `UI_HOOKS` in `shared/src/hooks.ts`, and this page, the comment at the top of the stylesheet `aubergine css new` writes, and the tests that hold the page to it are made from it.

**Not promised:** class names, test IDs (`data-testid`), how elements are nested, and anything not on this page. A rule that names a class may stop matching in any release.

An attribute selector is as specific as a class: a rule of yours on a part wins over the app’s own rule of the same specificity, because your file comes last. Where the app’s rule is more specific, match it, or add a part or an attribute to yours.

## Tokens

Every size, space, corner, layer, motion and color of the page is a custom property on `:root`. Set one there and everything that uses it follows; read one with `var(--name)`. The colors are given a value by each color theme, so set them under `:root[data-color-theme="<id>"]` or `:root[data-theme="dark"]` to change one theme or one kind only. [design.md](design.md) says what each is for.

- **Type: sizes, weights, line heights and the two font lists:** `--font-meta`, `--font-body`, `--font-title`, `--font-screen`, `--weight-normal`, `--weight-strong`, `--leading`, `--leading-heading`, `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`.
- **Space: the grid of four and the gutters:** `--space-1`, `--space-2`, `--space-3`, `--space-4`, `--space-6`, `--space-8`, `--gutter-panel`, `--gutter-card`, `--gutter-screen`.
- **Sizes of regions: the column of a page, the drawer, label columns:** `--page-width`, `--canvas-column-width`, `--drawer-width`, `--facts-label`, `--kind-column`, `--page-head`.
- **Corners:** `--radius-control`, `--radius-surface`, `--radius-pill`.
- **Heights of controls and chips:** `--control`, `--control-compact`, `--control-large`, `--chip`.
- **Motion: durations, the curve, how far what opens travels:** `--motion-quick`, `--motion-open`, `--motion-ease`, `--motion-busy`, `--motion-travel`.
- **Layers, lowest first:** `--z-canvas`, `--z-panel`, `--z-menu`, `--z-screen`, `--z-tour`, `--z-toast`.
- **Colors: every color theme gives each of these a value:** `--bg`, `--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--field`, `--surface-active`, `--border`, `--border-strong`, `--border-control`, `--text`, `--text-muted`, `--accent`, `--accent-soft`, `--accent-text`, `--on-accent`, `--attention`, `--attention-soft`, `--attention-text`, `--on-attention`, `--working`, `--working-soft`, `--working-text`, `--ok`, `--ok-soft`, `--ok-text`, `--danger`, `--danger-soft`, `--danger-text`, `--on-danger`, `--scrim`, `--shadow`, `--accent-pressed`, `--attention-pressed`, `--danger-pressed`, `--selection`, `--ring`, `--terminal-bg`, `--canvas-dot`, `--minimap-mask`, `--minimap-node`, `--qr-dark`, `--qr-light`.
- **Shadows, one for each layer that floats:** `--shadow-bar`, `--shadow-node`, `--shadow-menu`, `--shadow-dialog`.

## On the root

On `<html>`, for rules such as `:root[data-page="runs"] …` or `[data-server="linked"] …`.

| Attribute | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `data-theme` | `light` or `dark`: which kind the page is drawn as. There from the first paint. |
| `data-color-theme` | The built-in color theme drawn (for a theme file of your own, the one it is laid over). There from the first paint. |
| `data-color-theme-id` | The ID of the color theme drawn, a theme file’s own included. There from the first paint. |
| `data-page` | `canvas`, `library`, `workflows` or `runs`: what is shown under the top bar; `terminal` for a terminal in a browser tab of its own. Set once the page has loaded. |
| `data-project` | The ID of the project looked at. Set once the page has loaded. |
| `data-server` | `own` while the page shows the server that sent it, `linked` while it shows a server linked in this browser. Set once the page has loaded. |
| `data-here` | There while the page is used at the computer Aubergine runs on (not from another device, and not while a linked server is shown). |

## Parts

The stable pieces of the page carry `data-part`: `[data-part="terminal-title"]`.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `top-bar` | The bar at the top of the window: the app’s name, the project, the places, For you, Settings and Help. |
| `canvas-tabs` | The bar of canvas tabs over the canvas (or the column of canvases at the left, as the canvases are shown). |
| `canvas-tab` | One canvas’s tab, as tabs or in the column, and its dot on the folded column. |
| `side-panel` | The side panel, open or folded to its rail. |
| `terminal-list` | The list of terminals in the side panel. |
| `terminal-row` | One terminal’s row in that list. |
| `canvas` | The canvas: the surface the terminals and frames lie on. |
| `canvas-bar` | The bar over the canvas: Go to…, the map’s button, the view and the rest. |
| `map` | The map of the canvas, in its corner, while it is shown. |
| `terminal` | A terminal on the canvas: the whole box, its title, body and the note beside it. |
| `terminal-title` | A terminal’s title on the canvas: its state, its name, what it says after the name, its tools. |
| `terminal-body` | A terminal’s body on the canvas: the terminal itself, live or as a snapshot, or what is said once its shell has ended. |
| `terminal-note` | The note beside a terminal on the canvas: its summary and its log. |
| `frame` | A frame on the canvas, with its label. |
| `details` | The drawer beside the side panel: the details of one thing (a terminal, a run, a message thread). |
| `page` | A page shown in place of the canvas: Library, Workflows, Runs. |
| `dialog` | A dialog or a sheet over the page: Settings, Help, the review, a question. |
| `menu` | A menu, wherever it hangs from. |
| `toast` | The one place that says what just happened. |
| `focus-head` | The head of a terminal in a browser tab of its own (`/t/<terminal>`). |
| `focus-body` | The terminal itself in a browser tab of its own. |

## Attributes of a part

A terminal’s attributes are on each part that stands for one terminal (`terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head`), with the same values on all of them, so that one rule can match a terminal wherever it is drawn.

| Attribute | On | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-session` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | The terminal’s ID. |
| `data-name` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | The terminal’s name, as written: `[data-name^="prod"]`. |
| `data-state` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | Its state in one word, the same everywhere: `waiting` (for you), `processing`, `unread`, `failed`, `idle` or `ended`. |
| `data-tags` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | Its tags, in lowercase, separated by spaces: `[data-tags~="prod"]`. Empty when it has none. |
| `data-agent` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | There when an agent is on record in it, with the kind of agent (`claude-code`). |
| `data-color` | `terminal`, `terminal-row`, `focus-head` | Its color: a named one (`red`, `blue`…), `none`, or a color of your own as `#rrggbb`. |
| `data-selected` | `terminal`, `terminal-row` | `true` on the terminal that is selected: on the canvas while no other has the keyboard, in the list while its row is marked. |
| `data-focused` | `terminal`, `terminal-row` | `true` on the terminal that has the keyboard. |
| `data-theme-id` | `terminal-body`, `focus-body` | There where a terminal’s body is drawn in another color theme than the page: that theme’s ID. |
| `data-canvas` | `canvas-tab` | The canvas’s ID. |
| `data-current` | `canvas-tab` | `true` on the tab of the canvas being looked at. |

## Examples

The title of every terminal tagged prod in red, on the canvas and in a tab of its own:

```css
[data-part="terminal"][data-tags~="prod"] [data-part="terminal-title"],
[data-part="focus-head"][data-tags~="prod"] {
  background: #5c1f24;
}
```

No map on the canvas:

```css
[data-part="map"] {
  display: none;
}
```

Rounder corners everywhere, through a token:

```css
:root {
  --radius-surface: 16px;
  --radius-control: 10px;
}
```

A terminal waiting for you stands out in the list:

```css
[data-part="terminal-row"][data-state="waiting"] {
  font-weight: var(--weight-strong);
}
```

A quieter canvas in the dark: its dots in the color of the ground:

```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --canvas-dot: var(--bg);
}
```
